# The shade is a generated model, and the generated file is a source
Status: accepted (2026-10-14)
Code: tools/blender/sources/shade_tripo.glb, tools/blender/build_shade.py, tools/blender/make_textures.py, assets/models/shade.obj, assets/models/shade_hollow.obj, assets/textures/shade.png, assets/textures/shade_normal.png, src/game/NightMazeAppPasses.cpp, tests/ObjLoaderTests.cpp

Context: the shade was sixteen-sided rings with a flat hood, 518 triangles, and up close it read as a cone in a sheet. A robe with real folds, a deep hood and wide sleeves is beyond what I can write ring by ring, and every asset was a script.
Decision: the shade starts from a model Tripo generated, committed as it came (`shade_tripo.glb`, 2.86 MB). `build_shade.py` is still the source of the game files: it takes out the mannequin's hands by the colour of their texels, keeps the largest island, scales the figure to 2.2 m and sinks it 0.1 m, makes the picture dark blue and averages both pictures down to 1024 by 1024, puts a curved sheet of night in front of the mannequin's face and lids in the holes of the hands, and exports with the OBJ conventions of `docs/assets.md`. Two exceptions: the cloth has smooth normals (the loader reads `vn` as written), and it keeps the UVs of the source. A run gives the same bytes, also inside `make_all.py`, and `make_textures.py` no longer writes the pictures of the shade.
Why: I rejected committing only the cleaned files: then an output would be the source, and a change of size, colour or texture size would mean editing it by hand. The 0.1 m of hem under the ground stays: the steepest ground of the maze is 9.6 % (the heightmap at a height scale of 1), which is 5 cm over the 0.5 m to the edge of the pool, and the walk lifts the figure by up to 4 cm and its lean by 2 cm more at the back. The colour is chosen in the game: the flashlight is warm, and the first dark blue I tried, (0.28, 0.33, 0.62), read as neutral grey in its beam. I rejected making the mannequin's face itself the night: from the side it showed the profile of a head.
Cost and revisit: the cloth is 14,557 triangles and the hollow 1,184, where the old models had 518 and 24, and the two pictures are 304 and 355 kB. Measured on an RTX 4070 Ti (2026-10-14, Release, window of 1280 x 720, seed 6, the shade 4 m ahead): 96,793 triangles a frame against 50,304 before, the frame 0.65 against 0.59 ms, the moon shadow pass 0.056 against 0.045 ms, the flashlight shadow 0.020 against 0.018 ms and the scene 0.239 against 0.237 ms. That is one averaged reading of the Diagnostics category each: the triangle counts are exact, the times only a rough guide. On 68 triangles of the cloth (72 cm²) the normal map is upside down, and the loader warns about it on every start. I reopen it for a second generated model, or if the frame time of a slower card says the triangles matter.
